newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-THREE-WAY TIE AT QUAD CITY TOURNAMENT.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-THREE-WAY TIE AT QUAD CITY TOURNAMENT.

text.p: Larry Nelson, Charlie Rymer
and Joey Gullion fired 5-under-par 65s Thursday to share a
one-shot lead after the opening round of the $1.2 million Quad
City Classic golf tournament at the Oakwood Country Club.
Nelson, who won the 1987 PGA Championship, has 10 career
victories during a 25-year career on Tour. Rymer and Gullion
are seeking their first wins.
Denis Watson and Ed Fiori shot 4-under 66s and are one
stroke behind the leaders.
Six players are tied for sixth after opening-round 67s,
including Taylor Smith, Scott McCarron, Jeff Maggert, Brandel
Chamblee, Keith Fergus and Fred Funk.
Twenty-year-old Tiger Woods, playing in his third event as
a professional, shot a one-under-par 69 and is four shots off
the pace.
Defending champion D.A. Weibring posted a two-over-par 72
and trails by seven. He won the event last year after the
tournament was shortened to 54 holes due to rain. The Illinois
native won the Hartford Open earlier this year and is gunning
for his sixth career title. He also won the Quad City Classic
in 1979, his first title as a professional.
The field is watered down with many of the top American
and international professionals participating in the
Presidents Cup.
Woods is 204th on the money list entering the tournament
and needs to finish in the top 125 to remain on the PGA Tour
without having to attend qualifying school.
First prize is $180,000.
